subject: Terra boundary affirmation & private scope packet
messages:
From: Amrita Shah <security@horizonhealth.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Horizon Health Procurement <procurement@horizonhealth.com>
Date: Tue, 03 Jun 2025 13:23:00 +0000
Subject: Request: Hosted-region & VPC scope for Horizon pilot

Hi Marissa,

Thanks for the demo last week. As we prepare our procurement packet we need a concise technical/evidentiary packet showing the following for the pilot tenant:

- Clear statement that all content (prompts, responses, embeddings) for Horizon tenant will be hosted and processed only within EU jurisdiction (data-in-rest and data-in-motion).
- VPC/private endpoint topology and controls for a private deployment (diagram or network sketch).
- KMS/HSM key residency: can customer-managed keys be provisioned in EU region and kept there? Any scenarios where keys or plaintext might leave EU?
- List of SOC 2 / CAIQ artifacts you can include in a short packet (we don't need full SOC report, but excerpts/answers are helpful).
- Short fallback/DR statement: in an emergency will there ever be processing outside the EU? If so, what are the triggers and what data classes are affected?

If possible, please send a one-page statement we can attach to the PO plus the packet of artifacts (CAIQ slice, network diagram, and a short operational note on peering). We'd like these by EOD Friday (2025-06-06) to hit our legal review.

Thanks — happy to hop on a quick call if easier.

Amrita Shah
Manager, Security & Privacy
Horizon Health
security@horizonhealth.com

Attachment: none

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Amrita Shah <security@horizonhealth.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 03 Jun 2025 15:02:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Request: Hosted-region & VPC scope for Horizon pilot

Hi Amrita —

Thanks for the clear list. We've pulled together a compact packet and a one-paragraph legal-friendly statement you can attach to the PO. High-level summary below; full packet attached (terra_scope_packet.zip).

Summary answers:
- EU-only hosting: By default the tenant will be pinned to our EU hosting zone (primary AZs in eu-west-1 and eu-central-1 as configured for the pilot). All customer content (requests, responses, embeddings, caches stored to KV) will be stored and processed within the EU tenancy for normal operations.

- Private connectivity: The packet includes an annotated network diagram (network_annotated_diagram.png) showing the VPC endpoint model we will provision for Horizon: private endpoints, NAT controls, and peering routes. We support AWS PrivateLink and VPC peering; configuration options are listed in the diagram.

- KMS/HSM: We support customer-managed keys (CMKs) in the EU region. Customer KMS keys can be configured and kept in your AWS account (recommended). Redwood can also use a dedicated key in our EU-managed project if you prefer. We do not replicate plaintext outside the EU; key material remains in-region.

- SOC 2 / CAIQ: Included is a CAIQ excerpt (terra_caiq_excerpt.pdf) focused on hosting, network controls, and key management. We also include a short SOC 2 artifact checklist that maps controls to the pilot scope.

- Fallback/DR: Normal operations are EU-only. For planned maintenance we may route traffic within EU-only maintenance windows. For unplanned capacity failures we have a documented fallback policy: we will not process customer content in non-EU regions without prior written customer authorization except in narrowly defined emergency scenarios (e.g., full-region outage) — see the attached commitment statement for the exact legal-friendly sentence you can use in the PO.

Attachments in terra_scope_packet.zip:
- terra_caiq_excerpt.pdf (CAIQ answers slice)
- network_annotated_diagram.png (PNG)
- eu-hosting-commitment-statement.pdf (one-page statement)
- runbook-index.txt (list of runbook sections relevant to tenant isolation)

Next steps: please confirm whether you want CMKs in your account vs Redwood-managed EU key and whether you prefer PrivateLink or VPC peering. Happy to join legal/security call Thursday if helpful.

Best,

Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com
+1 415 555 0142

Attachment: terra_scope_packet.zip (contains CAIQ slice, diagram, statement)

From: Amrita Shah <security@horizonhealth.com>

Date: Wed, 04 Jun 2025 09:11:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Request: Hosted-region & VPC scope for Horizon pilot

Thanks Marissa — this is helpful. A couple quick clarifications after a fast pass through the packet: 

1) Fallback: your note says "we will not process customer content in non-EU regions without prior written customer authorization except in narrowly defined emergency scenarios (e.g., full-region outage)" — procurement needs a more explicit one-liner that we can drop into the PO that reads like a hard commitment. Can you provide that exact one-line sentence?

2) KV/Cache behavior: does your prefix/KV cache ever persist outside EU for performance reasons (edge caches, CDN, ephemeral cache nodes)? If yes, what data classes are cached and for how long?

3) KMS: If we provision CMKs in our AWS account, will Redwood ever create session keys or cache unencrypted payloads outside EU for request routing or tokenization?

Apologies for the granular asks — legal wants specific language. If you can send the PO-ready sentence and a short bullet answer to 2/3 we can close this packet quickly.

Thanks,
Amrita

Hi Amrita —

Thanks — answers below so your legal team can paste the exact language. We also attached the specific files to the packet and uploaded the same materials to the Drive link in case you want separate attachments for legal.

PO-ready sentence (copy/paste):
"Redwood Inference will process, store, and transmit customer content (including prompts, responses, embeddings, and derived artifacts) exclusively within the European Union for the Horizon Health tenant, and will not process or transfer such content to non-EU regions without prior written authorization from Horizon Health, except in the case of a documented, mutually-agreed emergency declared in writing by both parties to restore service availability following a complete EU-region outage."

KV/cache answer (short bullets):
- We operate only EU-located KV cache nodes for the Horizon tenant under normal operations; no edge caching of customer content will occur outside EU.
- We may use CDN/edge infrastructure for static assets (e.g., product UI resources) that do not contain customer content.
- Cache TTLs for model prefix/KV entries are configurable per-tenant; defaults are 24 hours for ephemeral inference caches, and 30 days for longer-term embeddings cache if enabled (all stored in EU).

KMS/session key answer:
- If Horizon provisions CMKs in your AWS account, all envelope encryption/decryption operations for protected content occur with keys that have key material resident in EU. Redwood may generate short-lived envelope keys for processing, but the envelope keys are themselves encrypted with the CMK and never expose plaintext outside EU. We do not persist unencrypted payloads outside EU.

Operational note: in the extremely unlikely event of a full EU-region outage we have an emergency runbook; any cross-region processing would require prior written consent unless both parties explicitly declare the emergency process in writing (see PO sentence above).

I've cc'd Karthik (infra) and Irene (security/compliance) in case legal wants a technical call to walk through the packet. If you'd like the one-liner reformatted for procurement's template we can paste that directly into the DocuSign/PO.

Best regards,

Marissa Cole
